answer: Neighborhood Cutoff Rule. Each node scores peers by how many of its other peers already connect to them; agents below a minimum shared-neighbor count get throttled to a low-bandwidth haven outside the main routing mesh. Honest clusters with dense local links pass easily, while a sybil farm's fresh identities share few genuine neighbors and stay isolated. The jade metric is the overlap ratio itself, visible per request.
